# ASSET PURCHASE AGREEMENT

This ASSET PURCHASE AGREEMENT (this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of October 30, 2026, by and between **Marrowind Packaging Corp.**, a New York corporation ("**Seller**"), and **Tessaly Holdings LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Buyer**"). Seller and Buyer are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Seller designs, manufactures, converts and sells corrugated packaging products, including corrugated sheets, boxes, displays and protective inserts (the "**Business**").

B. Seller wishes to sell and assign to Buyer, and Buyer wishes to purchase and assume from Seller, substantially all of the assets, and certain specified liabilities, of the Business, on the terms and subject to the conditions of this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants, representations, warranties and agreements in this Agreement, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## ARTICLE I. DEFINITIONS

**1.1 Defined Terms.** The following terms have the meanings set forth below:

(a) "**Affiliate**" of a Person means any other Person that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Person.

(b) "**Ancillary Agreements**" means the Transition Services Agreement, the Bill of Sale and the Escrow Agreement.

(c) "**Assumed Liabilities**" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.3.

(d) "**Bill of Sale**" means the Bill of Sale and Assignment and Assumption Agreement to be delivered by Seller and Buyer at the Closing.

(e) "**Business Day**" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or day on which banks in New York, New York are authorized or required by law to close.

(f) "**Closing**" and "**Closing Date**" have the meanings set forth in Section 3.1.

(g) "**Disclosure Schedule**" means the disclosure schedule delivered by Seller to Buyer concurrently with the execution of this Agreement.

(h) "**Escrow Agent**" means Corbel Trust Company, N.A.

(i) "**Escrow Agreement**" means the Indemnity Escrow Agreement to be entered into at the Closing among Seller, Buyer and the Escrow Agent.

(j) "**Escrow Amount**" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.6.

(k) "**Excluded Assets**" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.2.

(l) "**Excluded Liabilities**" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.4.

(m) "**Fundamental Representations**" means the representations and warranties in Section 4.1 (Organization and Good Standing), Section 4.2 (Authority; Enforceability), Section 4.5 (Title to Purchased Assets) and Section 4.12 (Brokers).

(n) "**Losses**" means losses, damages, liabilities, deficiencies, judgments, interest, awards, penalties, fines, costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees.

(o) "**Material Adverse Effect**" means any event, change or effect that is, individually or in the aggregate, materially adverse to the Purchased Assets or the results of operations or financial condition of the Business, other than effects arising from general economic conditions, changes in law or GAAP, or conditions generally affecting the corrugated packaging industry, in each case that do not disproportionately affect the Business.

(p) "**Person**" means any individual, corporation, limited liability company, partnership, trust, governmental authority or other entity.

(q) "**Purchase Price**" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.5.

(r) "**Purchased Assets**" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.1.

(s) "**Transition Services Agreement**" means the Transition Services Agreement to be entered into at the Closing between Seller and Buyer.

## ARTICLE II. PURCHASE AND SALE

**2.1 Purchased Assets.** At the Closing, Seller shall sell, assign, transfer, convey and deliver to Buyer, and Buyer shall purchase from Seller, free and clear of all liens other than permitted liens listed in Section 2.1 of the Disclosure Schedule, all of Seller's right, title and interest in all assets used or held for use in the Business, other than the Excluded Assets (the "**Purchased Assets**"). The Purchased Assets include:

(a) all inventory, raw materials (including linerboard and medium), work in process, finished goods and supplies;

(b) all machinery, corrugators, converting equipment, die cutters, printers, tooling, vehicles, furniture and other tangible personal property;

(c) all contracts listed in Section 2.1(c) of the Disclosure Schedule (the "**Assigned Contracts**");

(d) all intellectual property used or held for use in the Business, including customer dies and print plates;

(e) all accounts receivable arising from the Business;

(f) all permits, to the extent transferable; and

(g) all books, records, customer lists and supplier lists relating to the Business.

**2.2 Excluded Assets.** Notwithstanding Section 2.1, the Purchased Assets do not include, and Seller shall retain, the following assets (the "**Excluded Assets**"): Seller's cash, the Albany manufacturing facility, and the HOLLIS trademark.

**2.3 Assumed Liabilities.** At the Closing, Buyer shall assume and agree to pay, perform and discharge only (a) liabilities under the Assigned Contracts arising after the Closing, other than liabilities arising from any breach by Seller before the Closing, and (b) trade accounts payable of the Business incurred in the ordinary course and reflected in the Closing statement under Section 2.7 (together, the "**Assumed Liabilities**").

**2.4 Excluded Liabilities.** Buyer shall not assume, and Seller shall remain responsible for, all liabilities of Seller other than the Assumed Liabilities (the "**Excluded Liabilities**"), including all liabilities relating to the Excluded Assets, all pre-Closing taxes of Seller, and all liabilities arising from the employment of any Person by Seller before the Closing.

**2.5 Purchase Price.** The aggregate purchase price for the Purchased Assets is $18,400,000 (the "**Purc

hase Price**"), plus the assumption of the Assumed Liabilities, subject to adjustment under Section 2.7.

**2.6 Payment at Closing; Escrow.** At the Closing, Buyer shall pay the Purchase Price as follows:

(a) $1,840,000 (the "**Escrow Amount**") to the Escrow Agent by wire transfer of immediately available funds, to be held and disbursed in accordance with the Escrow Agreement as security for Seller's indemnification obligations under Article IX; and

(b) the balance of the Purchase Price, less the Escrow Amount, to Seller by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated in writing by Seller at least two Business Days before the Closing.

**2.7 Working Capital Adjustment.** Within 60 days after the Closing Date, Buyer shall deliver to Seller a statement of the net working capital of the Business as of the Closing. If the net working capital is less than $2,150,000, Seller shall pay the shortfall to Buyer; if it exceeds $2,150,000, Buyer shall pay the excess to Seller. Seller has 30 days to object to the statement. Disputes not resolved within 30 days after an objection shall be submitted to an independent accounting firm mutually selected by the Parties, whose determination shall be final and binding absent manifest error.

**2.8 Allocation.** The Purchase Price shall be allocated among the Purchased Assets in accordance with Section 1060 of the Internal Revenue Code, as set forth in an allocation schedule prepared by Buyer within 90 days after the Closing Date and reasonably acceptable to Seller.

## ARTICLE III. CLOSING

**3.1 Closing.** The closing of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the "**Closing**") shall take place remotely by electronic exchange of documents and signatures on November 20, 2026, or on such other date as the Parties may agree in writing (the date on which the Closing occurs, the "**Closing Date**"). The Closing shall be effective as of 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on the Closing Date.

**3.2 Seller Closing Deliveries.** At the Closing, Seller shall deliver to Buyer:

(a) the Bill of Sale, duly executed by Seller;

(b) the Transition Services Agreement, duly executed by Seller;

(c) the Escrow Agreement, duly executed by Seller;

(d) a certificate of the Secretary of Seller certifying board and shareholder resolutions authorizing this Agreement and the transactions contemplated by it;

(e) the third-party consents listed in Section 4.4 of the Disclosure Schedule; and

(f) an IRS Form W-9 of Seller.

**3.3 Buyer Closing Deliveries.** At the Closing, Buyer shall deliver:

(a) the payments described in Section 2.6;

(b) the Bill of Sale, the Transition Services Agreement and the Escrow Agreement, each duly executed by Buyer; and

(c) a certificate of an authorized officer of Buyer certifying resolutions of Buyer authorizing this Agreement.

## ARTICLE IV. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF SELLER

Except as set forth in the Disclosure Schedule, Seller represents and warrants to Buyer as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as follows:

**4.1 Organization and Good Standing.** Seller is a corporation duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the State of New York.

**4.2 Authority; Enforceability.** Seller has full corporate power and authority to execute and deliver this Agreement and the Ancillary Agreements to which it is a party and to perform its obligations under them. This Agreement constitutes a legal, valid and binding obligation of Seller, enforceable in accordance with its terms.

**4.3 No Conflicts.** The execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by Seller do not violate Seller's organizational documents, any applicable law, or any material contract to which Seller is a party.

**4.4 Consents.** Section 4.4 of the Disclosure Schedule lists each consent required to assign the Assigned Contracts to Buyer.

**4.5 Title to Purchased Assets.** Seller has good and valid title to, or a valid leasehold interest in, all of the Purchased Assets, free and clear of all liens other than permitted liens.

**4.6 Condition of Assets.** The tangible Purchased Assets are in good operating condition and repair, ordinary wear and tear excepted, and are adequate for the uses to which they are being put.

**4.7 Financial Statements.** The audited balance sheet of the Business as of December 31, 2025, and the unaudited balance sheet as of September 30, 2026, together with the related statements of income, fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Business as of their dates, in accordance with GAAP consistently applied.

**4.8 Material Contracts.** Section 4.8 of the Disclosure Schedule lists each contract of the Business involving annual payments in excess of $150,000. Each such contract is valid and in full force, and neither Seller nor, to Seller's knowledge, any counterparty is in material breach.

**4.9 Intellectual Property.** The operation of the Business does not infringe the intellectual property of any Person, and, to Seller's knowledge, no Person is infringing the intellectual property included in the Purchased Assets.

**4.10 Compliance with Laws; Environmental Matters.** The Business is conducted in material compliance with applicable laws, including environmental laws, and Seller holds all material permits required to operate the Business.

**4.11 Litigation.** There is no action pending or, to Seller's knowledge, threatened against Seller relating to the Business or the Purchased Assets.

**4.12 Brokers.** No broker, finder or investment banker is entitled to any fee or commission in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement based on arrangements made by Seller.

## ARTICLE V. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF BUYER

Buyer represents and warrants to Seller as follows:

**5.1 Organization.** Buyer is a limited liability company duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of

 the State of Delaware.

**5.2 Authority.** Buyer has full power and authority to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement and the Ancillary Agreements to which it is a party.

**5.3 Sufficiency of Funds.** Buyer has, and at the Closing will have, sufficient immediately available funds to pay the Purchase Price.

**5.4 Brokers.** No broker or finder is entitled to any fee in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement based on arrangements made by Buyer.

## ARTICLE VI. COVENANTS

**6.1 Conduct of Business Before Closing.** From the date of this Agreement until the Closing, Seller shall operate the Business in the ordinary course consistent with past practice, maintain the Purchased Assets in good condition, and use commercially reasonable efforts to preserve relationships with customers, suppliers and employees.

**6.2 Access to Information.** Before the Closing, Seller shall give Buyer and its representatives reasonable access during normal business hours to the properties, books and records of the Business.

**6.3 Efforts; Consents.** Each Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to satisfy the conditions to Closing, and Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain the consents listed in Section 4.4 of the Disclosure Schedule.

**6.4 Employees.** Buyer shall offer employment, effective on the Closing Date, to the employees of the Business listed in Section 6.4 of the Disclosure Schedule on terms substantially comparable in the aggregate to their current terms.

**6.5 Non-Competition.** For three years after the Closing Date, Seller shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in the manufacture or sale of corrugated packaging products within the United States, except through the ownership of the Excluded Assets in a manner that does not compete with the Business.

**6.6 Transition Services.** At the Closing, Seller and Buyer shall enter into the Transition Services Agreement, under which Seller shall provide certain services to Buyer for a term of six months after the Closing Date.

**6.7 Further Assurances.** Following the Closing, each Party shall execute and deliver such additional documents and take such further actions as may be reasonably required to carry out the provisions of this Agreement.

## ARTICLE VII. CONDITIONS TO CLOSING

**7.1 Conditions to Buyer's Obligations.** Buyer's obligation to close is subject to: (a) the representations and warranties of Seller being true and correct in all material respects as of the Closing Date; (b) Seller having performed in all material respects its covenants required to be performed before Closing; (c) no Material Adverse Effect having occurred; and (d) delivery of the items in Section 3.2.

**7.2 Conditions to Seller's Obligations.** Seller's obligation to close is subject to: (a) the representations and warranties of Buyer being true and correct in all material respects as of the Closing Date; (b) Buyer having performed in all material respects its covenants required to be performed before Closing; and (c) delivery of the items in Section 3.3.

## ARTICLE VIII. TERMINATION

**8.1 Termination.** This Agreement may be terminated before the Closing: (a) by mutual written consent; (b) by either Party if the Closing has not occurred by December 31, 2026, provided the terminating Party's breach is not the principal cause of the failure to close; or (c) by either Party upon a material breach by the other Party that is not cured within 15 days after written notice.

**8.2 Effect of Termination.** Upon termination, this Agreement shall become void without liability of any Party, except for liability for willful breach before termination and except that Article X shall survive.

## ARTICLE IX. INDEMNIFICATION

**9.1 Survival.** The representations and warranties in this Agreement survive the Closing until the date that is 18 months after the Closing Date, except that the Fundamental Representations survive until 60 days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. Covenants survive in accordance with their terms. A claim asserted in writing with reasonable specificity before the end of the applicable survival period survives until finally resolved.

**9.2 Indemnification by Seller.** From and after the Closing, Seller shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Buyer and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, managers and employees, from and against all Losses arising out of or relating to:

(a) any breach of or inaccuracy in any representation or warranty made by Seller in this Agreement or in any certificate delivered by Seller under this Agreement;

(b) any breach of any covenant or agreement of Seller in this Agreement; and

(c) any Excluded Asset or Excluded Liability.

**9.3 Indemnification by Buyer.** From and after the Closing, Buyer shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Seller and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors and employees, from and against all Losses arising out of or relating to: (a) any breach of or inaccuracy in any representation or warranty made by Buyer in this Agreement; (b) any breach of any covenant or agreement of Buyer in this Agreement; and (c) any Assumed Liability.

**9.4 Limitations.**

(a) *Cap.* The aggregate liability of Seller under Section 9.2 shall not exceed 10% of the Purchase Price.

(b) *Basket.* Seller shall not be liable under Section 9.2(a) until the aggregate Losses exceed $184,000, after which Seller shall be liable only for Losses in excess of that amount.

(c) *Exceptions.* The limitations set forth in Section 9.4(a) and Section 9.4(b) shall not apply to any claim under Section 9.2(a), or to any claim arising from fraud.

(d) *Buyer Cap.* The aggregate liability of Buyer under Section 9.3(a) shall not exceed 10% of the Purchase Price.

(e) *Insurance.* Losses shall be calculated net of any insurance proceeds actually received by the Indemnified Party in respect of the applicable claim.

**9.5 Cla

ims Procedure.** A Party seeking indemnification (the "**Indemnified Party**") shall give prompt written notice to the Party from whom indemnification is sought (the "**Indemnifying Party**") describing the claim in reasonable detail. Failure to give prompt notice relieves the Indemnifying Party of its obligations only to the extent it is materially prejudiced. The Indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any third-party claim with counsel reasonably acceptable to the Indemnified Party and shall not settle any such claim without the Indemnified Party's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, unless the settlement involves only the payment of money and includes a full release of the Indemnified Party.

**9.6 Source of Recovery.** Any amount payable to a Buyer indemnitee under Section 9.2 shall be satisfied first from the funds then held by the Escrow Agent under the Escrow Agreement and thereafter directly by Seller.

**9.7 Escrow Release.** The Escrow Agent shall release the remaining Escrow Amount, less the amount of any pending claims, to Seller 18 months after the Closing Date, in accordance with the Escrow Agreement.

**9.8 Exclusive Remedy.** Except for claims arising from fraud and claims for specific performance or injunctive relief, the indemnification provided in this Article IX is the sole and exclusive remedy of the Parties for any breach of the representations, warranties, covenants and agreements in this Agreement.

**9.9 Tax Treatment.** All indemnification payments shall be treated as adjustments to the Purchase Price for tax purposes, unless otherwise required by law.

## ARTICLE X. MISCELLANEOUS

**10.1 Expenses.** Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement, each Party shall bear its own costs and expenses incurred in connection with this Agreement. Transfer taxes arising from the transfer of the Purchased Assets shall be borne equally by Seller and Buyer.

**10.2 Notices.** All notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and are deemed given when delivered personally, one Business Day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier, or when sent by email with confirmation of transmission, to the addresses below (or such other address as a Party designates by notice):

If to Seller: Marrowind Packaging Corp., 410 Riverside Industrial Parkway, Rochester, New York 14606, Attention: Chief Executive Officer.

If to Buyer: Tessaly Holdings LLC, 1200 Market Street, Suite 900, Wilmington, Delaware 19801, Attention: General Counsel.

**10.3 Amendment; Waiver.** This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties. No waiver is effective unless in writing and signed by the Party against whom it is asserted.

**10.4 Assignment.** Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that Buyer may assign its rights to an Affiliate or, for collateral purposes, to its lenders, provided Buyer remains liable for its obligations.

**10.5 Successors and Assigns.** This Agreement binds and benefits the Parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns.

**10.6 No Third-Party Beneficiaries.** Except for the indemnitees under Article IX, nothing in this Agreement confers any right or remedy on any Person other than the Parties.

**10.7 Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force, and the invalid provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable.

**10.8 Governing Law.** This Agreement, and all claims or causes of action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the Laws of the State of New York, without giving effect to any choice or conflict of law provision or rule that would cause the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

**10.9 Jurisdiction.** Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the State and federal courts located in New York County, New York for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts, including any objection based on inconvenient forum.

**10.10 Waiver of Jury Trial.** EACH PARTY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT.

**10.11 Specific Performance.** The Parties agree that irreparable damage would occur if any provision of this Agreement were not performed in accordance with its terms, and that each Party is entitled to specific performance and injunctive relief, in addition to any other remedy.

**10.12 Order of Precedence.** In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and any Ancillary Agreement, this Agreement controls over the Ancillary Agreements, except that each Ancillary Agreement controls as to its specific subject matter.

**10.13 Counterparts; Electronic Signatures.** This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. Signatures delivered by email in PDF format or by electronic signature service are effective as originals.

**10.14 Interpretation.** Headings are for convenience only. The words "include" and "including" are deemed followed by "without limitation." References to Articles, Sections and Schedules are to those of this Agreement unless otherwise stated.

# TRANSITION SERVICES AGREEMENT

This TRANSITION SERVICES AGREEMENT (this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of November 20, 2026, by and between **Marrowind Packaging Corp.**, a New York corporation ("**Seller**"), and **Tessaly Holdings LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Buyer**"). Seller and Buyer are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Seller and Buyer are parties to an Asset Purchase Agreement dated as of October 30, 2026 (the "**Purchase Agreement**"). Under the Purchase Agreement, Buyer is acquiring the Purchased Assets and assuming the Assumed Liabilities of the Business.

B. Section 6.6 of the Purchase Agreement requires the Parties to enter into this Agreement at the Closing. Under this Agreement, Seller will provide certain transitional services to Buyer so that Buyer can operate the Business in an orderly manner after the Closing.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Agreement and in the Purchase Agreement, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

**1.1 Defined Terms.** Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Agreement have the meanings given to them in the Purchase Agreement. In addition:

(a) "**Service Coordinator**" has the meaning set forth in Section 3.4.

(b) "**Service Fees**" means the fees for the Services set forth in Schedule A.

(c) "**Service Recipient Data**" means all data and records relating to the Business that Seller processes, stores or generates in providing the Services.

(d) "**Services**" means the transitional services described in Schedule A, together with any Additional Services agreed under Section 3.3.

(e) "**Term**" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.1.

## 2. TERM AND TERMINATION

**2.1 Term.** This Agreement begins on the Closing Date and continues until the date that is 6 months after the Closing Date (the "**Term**"). The Term may end earlier under Section 2.2 or Section 2.3.

**2.2 Early Termination of Individual Services by Buyer.** Buyer may terminate any Service, in whole or in part, by giving Seller at least 30 days' written notice. The Service Fees for a terminated Service end on the effective date of termination. If a Service was paid in advance, Seller shall refund the prorated unused portion within 30 days.

**2.3 Termination for Breach.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within 30 days after receiving written notice of it. If the breach is a failure to pay undisputed Service Fees, the cure period is 15 days.

**2.4 Effect of Termination.** When this Agreement or any Service terminates:

(a) Buyer shall pay all Service Fees accrued through the effective date of termination; and

(b) Seller shall deliver to Buyer all Service Recipient Data relating to the terminated Services, in the format in which Seller maintains it or another format reasonably requested by Buyer.

Sections 2.4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement.

## 3. SERVICES

**3.1 Provision of Services.** During the Term, Seller shall provide, or cause its Affiliates or third-party contractors to provide, the Services to Buyer. Seller remains responsible for the performance of any Affiliate or contractor it uses.

**3.2 Standard of Performance.** Seller shall provide each Service substantially as follows:

(a) in a manner, scope, nature, priority and quality consistent with how Seller provided the Service to the Business during the 12 months before the Closing Date; and

(b) with at least the same degree of care Seller uses for its own operations.

Seller is not required to provide any Service at a volume materially greater than the volume provided to the Business during that 12-month period unless the Parties agree otherwise in writing.

**3.3 Additional Services.** Buyer may ask Seller to provide services that are not described in Schedule A but that Seller provided to the Business during the 12 months before the Closing Date ("**Additional Services**"). Seller shall consider each request in good faith. Any Additional Services and their fees shall be documented in a written amendment to Schedule A signed by both Parties.

**3.4 Service Coordinators.** Each Party shall designate an individual to act as its primary contact for the administration of this Agreement (each, a "**Service Coordinator**"). Seller's initial Service Coordinator is its Vice President, Finance. Buyer's initial Service Coordinator is its Director of Integration. Either Party may replace its Service Coordinator by written notice. The Service Coordinators shall meet, in person or by video conference, at least every two weeks during the Term.

**3.5 Migration Assistance.** During the Term, Seller shall cooperate reasonably with Buyer to transition each Service to Buyer or to Buyer's designated provider. This includes giving reasonable access to Seller personnel who are knowledgeable about the Services. Buyer shall reimburse Seller's reasonable, documented out-of-pocket costs of this cooperation.

**3.6 Third-Party Consents.** If providing a Service requires the consent of a third party, Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain that consent. Buyer shall bear the reasonable, documented cost of obtaining it, subject to prior written approval by Buyer. If the consent cannot be obtained, the Parties shall cooperate in good faith to find a reasonable alternative arrangement.

## 4. BUYER OBLIGATIONS

**4.1 Cooperation.** Buyer shall provide Seller with information, access and cooperation reasonably necessary for Seller to perform the Services.

**4.2 Systems Access.** If Buyer personnel are given access to Seller's information technology systems, Buyer shall ensure that those personnel:

(a) comply with Seller's written security and acceptable-use policies

transition_services_agreement.md, page 2 of 3:
 that have been provided to Buyer; and

(b) use the access solely to receive the Services.

## 5. FEES AND PAYMENT

**5.1 Service Fees.** Buyer shall pay Seller the Service Fees for each Service as set forth in Schedule A. The Service Fees are intended to reflect Seller's fully loaded cost of providing the Services, without markup.

**5.2 Invoicing and Payment.** Seller shall invoice Buyer monthly in arrears. Each invoice shall itemize the Service Fees and any reimbursable expenses. Buyer shall pay each undisputed invoice within 30 days after receipt, by wire transfer to an account designated by Seller.

**5.3 Disputed Invoices.** If Buyer disputes any invoice in good faith, Buyer shall:

(a) notify Seller in writing of the disputed amount and the basis for the dispute within 20 days after receipt of the invoice; and

(b) pay the undisputed portion when due.

The Service Coordinators shall attempt to resolve the dispute within 15 days after the notice.

**5.4 Taxes.** Buyer shall pay any sales, use or similar taxes imposed on the Services, other than taxes based on Seller's income.

**5.5 Late Payment.** Undisputed amounts not paid when due accrue interest at the rate of 1% per month, or the maximum rate permitted by law if lower, from the due date until paid.

## 6. CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA

**6.1 Confidentiality.** Each Party shall keep confidential all non-public information of the other Party that it receives under this Agreement. Each Party shall use that information only to perform or receive the Services. These obligations do not apply to information that:

(a) is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this Agreement;

(b) was lawfully known to the receiving Party before disclosure;

(c) is independently developed by the receiving Party; or

(d) must be disclosed under law or court order, provided that the receiving Party gives prompt notice to the disclosing Party where legally permitted.

**6.2 Service Recipient Data.** As between the Parties, all Service Recipient Data is owned by Buyer as part of the Purchased Assets. Seller shall:

(a) maintain the Service Recipient Data using reasonable administrative, physical and technical safeguards;

(b) not use it except to provide the Services; and

(c) return or destroy it, at Buyer's election, within 30 days after the end of the Term.

## 7. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION

**7.1 Disclaimer.** Except as expressly provided in this Agreement, Seller makes no representations or warranties, express or implied, regarding the Services. This includes any implied warranty of merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose.

**7.2 Limitation of Liability.** Neither Party is liable to the other for any consequential, special, indirect or punitive damages arising out of this Agreement, except in the case of gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of Section 6. Seller's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the total Service Fees paid and payable under this Agreement, except in the case of gross negligence or willful misconduct.

**7.3 Indemnification.** Each Party shall indemnify the other Party against Losses arising from third-party claims to the extent caused by the indemnifying Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct in performing or receiving the Services. The procedures in Section 9.5 of the Purchase Agreement apply to these claims, with necessary changes.

## 8. FORCE MAJEURE

**8.1 Force Majeure.** Neither Party is liable for any failure or delay in performance, other than payment obligations, to the extent caused by events beyond its reasonable control. Such events include acts of God, fire, flood, pandemic, war, terrorism, labor disputes not involving the affected Party's own employees, or failure of public utilities. The affected Party shall promptly notify the other Party and use commercially reasonable efforts to resume performance. Service Fees for any affected Service are suspended for the period during which the Service is not provided.

## 9. MISCELLANEOUS

# BILL OF SALE AND ASSIGNMENT AND ASSUMPTION AGREEMENT

This BILL OF SALE AND ASSIGNMENT AND ASSUMPTION AGREEMENT (this "**Bill of Sale**") is made and entered into as of November 20, 2026, by and between **Marrowind Packaging Corp.**, a New York corporation ("**Seller**"), and **Tessaly Holdings LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Buyer**"). Seller and Buyer are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Seller and Buyer are parties to an Asset Purchase Agreement dated as of October 30, 2026 (the "**Purchase Agreement**"). Under the Purchase Agreement, Seller has agreed to sell, assign, transfer, convey and deliver the Purchased Assets to Buyer. Buyer has agreed to purchase the Purchased Assets and to assume the Assumed Liabilities.

B. Section 3.2(a) and Section 3.3(b) of the Purchase Agreement require the Parties to execute and deliver this Bill of Sale at the Closing.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the payment of the Purchase Price, the mutual covenants in the Purchase Agreement, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

**1.1 Defined Terms.** Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Bill of Sale have the meanings given to them in the Purchase Agreement. In addition, the following terms have the meanings set forth below:

(a) "**Assigned Contracts**" means the contracts listed in Section 2.1(c) of the Disclosure Schedule.

(b) "**Purchased Assets**" means all of Seller's right, title and interest in, to and under all assets, properties and rights of every kind and nature, whether real, personal or mixed, tangible or intangible, wherever located, used or held for use in the Business. This includes:

> (i) all inventory, raw materials (including linerboard and medium), work in process, finished goods and supplies;
>
> (ii) all machinery, corrugators, converting equipment, die cutters, printers, tooling, vehicles, furniture and other tangible personal property;
>
> (iii) the Assigned Contracts;
>
> (iv) all intellectual property, including trademarks, trade names, customer dies and print plates;
>
> (v) all accounts receivable;
>
> (vi) all permits, to the extent transferable; and
>
> (vii) all books, records, customer lists and supplier lists relating to the Business.

**1.2 Interpretation.** Headings are for convenience only. The words "include" and "including" are deemed followed by "without limitation."

## 2. CONVEYANCE OF PURCHASED ASSETS

**2.1 Sale and Transfer.** Effective as of 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on the Closing Date, Seller hereby irrevocably sells, assigns, transfers, conveys and delivers to Buyer, and Buyer hereby accepts, all of the Purchased Assets. The Purchased Assets are conveyed free and clear of all liens other than permitted liens listed in Section 2.1 of the Disclosure Schedule.

**2.2 Delivery of Possession.** Seller shall deliver possession of the tangible Purchased Assets to Buyer at the locations where those assets are located on the Closing Date.

**2.3 Power of Attorney.** Seller hereby constitutes and appoints Buyer, and its successors and assigns, as Seller's true and lawful attorney-in-fact, with full power of substitution, in the name of Seller but on behalf and for the benefit of Buyer, to:

(a) demand and receive any of the Purchased Assets;

(b) give receipts and releases for and in respect of the Purchased Assets;

(c) institute and prosecute any proceedings that Buyer considers proper to collect, assert or enforce any claim, right or title of any kind in or to the Purchased Assets; and

(d) endorse, without recourse, any checks or other instruments payable to Seller in respect of the Purchased Assets.

Seller acknowledges that this power is coupled with an interest and is irrevocable.

## 3. ASSIGNMENT AND ASSUMPTION

**3.1 Assignment of Assigned Contracts.** Effective as of the Closing, Seller hereby assigns, transfers and conveys to Buyer all of Seller's right, title and interest in, to and under the Assigned Contracts.

**3.2 Assumption of Assumed Liabilities.** Effective as of the Closing, Buyer hereby accepts the assignment in Section 3.1 and assumes and agrees to pay, perform and discharge, when due, the Assumed Liabilities.

**3.3 Excluded Liabilities.** Buyer does not assume, and shall have no responsibility for, any Excluded Liability. Seller shall remain responsible for all Excluded Liabilities.

**3.4 Non-Assignable Contracts.** This Bill of Sale does not assign any Assigned Contract if an attempted assignment without the consent of a third party would constitute a breach of it, until that consent is obtained. Until then, Seller shall hold the Assigned Contract for the benefit of Buyer. Seller shall cooperate with Buyer in any reasonable arrangement designed to provide Buyer with the benefits of it. Buyer shall perform Seller's obligations under that contract arising after the Closing, to the extent those obligations would have been Assumed Liabilities. Seller shall continue to use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain the consents listed in Section 4.4 of the Disclosure Schedule, as required by Section 6.3 of the Purchase Agreement.

## 4. FURTHER ASSURANCES

**4.1 Further Actions.** From time to time after the Closing, at Buyer's request and without further consideration, Seller shall execute and deliver such further instruments of sale, conveyance, transfer and assignment, and take such other actions, as Buyer may reasonably request to vest in Buyer title to the Purchased Assets. These may include separate assignments of intellectual property for recording with the United States Patent and Trademark Office and certificates of title for vehicles.

**4.2 Receipt of Payments.** If Seller receives any payment, remittance or other amount in respect of any Purchased Asset after the Closing, Seller shall hold it in trust for Buyer. Seller shall pay it over to Buyer within 10 Business

# INDEMNITY ESCROW AGREEMENT

This INDEMNITY ESCROW AGREEMENT (this "**Escrow Agreement**") is entered into as of November 20, 2026, by and among **Marrowind Packaging Corp.**, a New York corporation ("**Seller**"), **Tessaly Holdings LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Buyer**"), and **Corbel Trust Company, N.A.**, a national banking association, as escrow agent (the "**Escrow Agent**"). Seller, Buyer and the Escrow Agent are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Seller and Buyer are parties to an Asset Purchase Agreement dated as of October 30, 2026 (the "**Purchase Agreement**"). Under the Purchase Agreement, Buyer is acquiring the Purchased Assets and assuming the Assumed Liabilities of the Business for a Purchase Price of $18,400,000.

B. Section 2.6(a) of the Purchase Agreement requires Buyer to deposit $1,840,000 of the Purchase Price with the Escrow Agent at the Closing. The deposit serves as security for Seller's indemnification obligations under Article IX of the Purchase Agreement.

C. Section 3.2(c) and Section 3.3(b) of the Purchase Agreement require Seller and Buyer to execute and deliver this Escrow Agreement at the Closing. The Escrow Agent is willing to act as escrow agent on the terms of this Escrow Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Escrow Agreement, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

**1.1 Defined Terms.** Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Escrow Agreement have the meanings given to them in the Purchase Agreement. In addition:

(a) "**Claim Notice**" has the meaning set forth in Section 3.1.

(b) "**Escrow Account**" means the segregated account established by the Escrow Agent under Section 2.2.

(c) "**Escrow Funds**" means, at any time, the Escrow Amount deposited under Section 2.1, together with all interest and other earnings on it, less all amounts distributed from the Escrow Account under this Escrow Agreement.

(d) "**Final Order**" means a final, non-appealable order or judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction, accompanied by a certificate of counsel for the presenting Party stating that the order or judgment is final and non-appealable.

(e) "**Joint Written Instructions**" means written instructions to the Escrow Agent signed by an authorized representative of each of Seller and Buyer.

(f) "**Objection Notice**" has the meaning set forth in Section 3.2.

(g) "**Release Date**" has the meaning set forth in Section 4.1.

## 2. APPOINTMENT; DEPOSIT; INVESTMENT

**2.1 Appointment and Deposit.** Seller and Buyer appoint the Escrow Agent to act as escrow agent under this Escrow Agreement. The Escrow Agent accepts the appointment. On the Closing Date, Buyer shall deposit with the Escrow Agent $1,840,000 (the "**Escrow Amount**") by wire transfer of immediately available funds. The Escrow Agent shall confirm receipt of the Escrow Amount to Seller and Buyer in writing promptly after receipt.

**2.2 Escrow Account.** The Escrow Agent shall hold the Escrow Funds in a segregated account in its name as escrow agent for the benefit of Seller and Buyer. The Escrow Agent shall hold and disburse the Escrow Funds only as provided in this Escrow Agreement. The Escrow Funds are not subject to any lien, attachment or other judicial process of any creditor of any Party, except as provided in a Final Order.

**2.3 Investment.** The Escrow Agent shall invest the Escrow Funds in a United States Treasury money market fund or interest-bearing deposit account of the Escrow Agent insured to the extent available by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, as Seller and Buyer jointly designate in Schedule B. Seller and Buyer may change the investment by Joint Written Instructions. The Escrow Agent is not liable for any loss resulting from an investment made in accordance with this Section 2.3, or from the liquidation of any investment needed to make a disbursement under this Escrow Agreement.

**2.4 Tax Matters.** For U.S. federal and applicable state income tax purposes, Buyer is treated as the owner of the Escrow Funds until they are distributed, consistent with Proposed Treasury Regulation Section 1.468B-8. All interest and other earnings on the Escrow Funds shall be reported to Buyer on IRS Form 1099 or other applicable form. Before the Closing Date, each of Seller and Buyer shall deliver to the Escrow Agent a properly completed IRS Form W-9. The Escrow Agent may withhold any tax required by law to be withheld from distributions under this Escrow Agreement.

## 3. CLAIMS AGAINST THE ESCROW FUNDS

**3.1 Claim Notice.** If Buyer, on its own behalf or on behalf of any other Buyer indemnitee, asserts a claim for indemnification under Section 9.2 of the Purchase Agreement, Buyer may deliver to the Escrow Agent and Seller, on or before the Release Date, a written notice (a "**Claim Notice**"). Each Claim Notice shall state:

(a) the amount of Losses claimed, or a good-faith estimate of them if they are not yet determinable; and

(b) in reasonable detail, the nature of the claim and the provision of the Purchase Agreement on which it is based.

**3.2 Objection Notice.** Seller may object to all or any part of a claim set out in a Claim Notice by delivering a written notice of objection to the Escrow Agent and Buyer within 30 days after Seller's receipt of the Claim Notice (an "**Objection Notice**"). Each Objection Notice shall specify the amount in dispute and the basis for the objection in reasonable detail.

**3.3 Payment of Uncontested Amounts.** If the Escrow Agent does not receive an Objection Notice within the 30-day period in Section 3.2, then on the fifth Business Day after the end of that period the Escrow Agent shall pay to Buyer, from the Escrow Funds, the amount claimed in the Claim Notice. If an Objection Notice disputes only part of a claim, the Escrow Agent

shall pay the undisputed portion to Buyer within five Business Days after receiving the Objection Notice.

**3.4 Disputed Amounts.** The Escrow Agent shall continue to hold any amount disputed in an Objection Notice until it receives either:

(a) Joint Written Instructions directing the disposition of that amount; or

(b) a Final Order directing the disposition of that amount.

The Escrow Agent shall disburse the disputed amount in accordance with the Joint Written Instructions or Final Order within five Business Days after receiving it.

**3.5 Estimated Claims.** If a Claim Notice states an estimated amount, Buyer may later deliver an updated Claim Notice to the Escrow Agent and Seller stating the amount of Losses as finally determined. Sections 3.2 through 3.4 apply to the updated Claim Notice.

**3.6 Insufficient Funds.** If the Escrow Funds are insufficient to pay any claim in full, the Escrow Agent shall pay the amount available. The Escrow Agent has no responsibility for any such remaining amount.

## 4. RELEASE OF ESCROW FUNDS

**4.1 Release Date.** On the date that is 18 months after the Closing Date (the "**Release Date**"), or if that date is not a Business Day, on the next Business Day, the Escrow Agent shall release to Seller the Escrow Funds then remaining, less the aggregate amount of all claims stated in Claim Notices delivered on or before the Release Date that have not been paid or resolved as of the Release Date (the "**Pending Claims Amount**").

**4.2 Release of Pending Claims Amount.** The Escrow Agent shall continue to hold the Pending Claims Amount after the Release Date. When each pending claim is resolved under Section 3, the Escrow Agent shall:

(a) pay to Buyer the amount, if any, due to Buyer on that claim; and

(b) release to Seller the amount, if any, by which the portion of the Pending Claims Amount held for that claim exceeds the amount paid to Buyer.

**4.3 Joint Written Instructions.** Notwithstanding any other provision of this Escrow Agreement, the Escrow Agent shall disburse Escrow Funds at any time in accordance with Joint Written Instructions.

**4.4 Method of Payment.** All disbursements shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by the recipient in Schedule A, or in a later written notice signed by the recipient and delivered to the Escrow Agent. The Escrow Agent is not a party to, and has no duty to inquire into the terms of, the Purchase Agreement or any other agreement between Seller and Buyer.

**5.2 Reliance.** The Escrow Agent may rely on any written notice, instruction or signature that it believes in good faith to be genuine and to have been signed or presented by the proper Person. The Escrow Agent may consult with counsel of its choice and is not liable for any action taken or omitted in good faith in accordance with that counsel's advice.

**5.3 Limitation of Liability.** The Escrow Agent is not liable for any action taken or omitted under this Escrow Agreement, except to the extent caused by its gross negligence or willful misconduct. In no event is the Escrow Agent liable for any special, indirect, consequential or punitive damages.

**5.4 Indemnification of Escrow Agent.** Seller and Buyer, jointly and severally, shall indemnify the Escrow Agent against any loss, liability, claim or expense, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising out of its performance under this Escrow Agreement, except to the extent caused by its gross negligence or willful misconduct. As between Seller and Buyer, each shall bear one-half of any amount payable under this Section 5.4. A Party whose conduct gave rise to the indemnified amount shall bear all of it.

**5.5 Fees and Expenses.** The Escrow Agent is entitled to the fees set forth in Schedule C, together with reimbursement of its reasonable, documented out-of-pocket expenses. Seller and Buyer shall each pay one-half of those fees and expenses.

**5.6 Conflicting Demands.** If the Escrow Agent receives conflicting demands or instructions concerning the Escrow Funds, it may refrain from acting until it receives Joint Written Instructions or a Final Order. It may also deposit the disputed Escrow Funds with a court of competent jurisdiction described in Section 7.2 and file an action in interpleader.

**5.7 Resignation and Removal.** The Escrow Agent may resign by giving Seller and Buyer at least 30 days' written notice. Seller and Buyer may remove the Escrow Agent by Joint Written Instructions delivered at least 30 days before the effective date of removal. Seller and Buyer shall appoint a successor escrow agent by Joint Written Instructions. The resignation or removal becomes effective when the successor accepts its appointment in writing and the Escrow Agent delivers the Escrow Funds to it. If no successor has been appointed within 30 days after the notice, the Escrow Agent may petition a court of competent jurisdiction described in Section 7.2 to appoint one.
